questions.question: The base of a right prism is a trapezium whose the length of parallel sides are 25 cm and 11 cm and the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides is 16 cm. If the height of the prism is 10 cm, then the volume of the prism is:
questions.questionHtml: The base of a right prism is a trapezium whose the length of parallel sides are 25 cm and 11 cm and the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides is 16 cm. If the height of the prism is 10 cm, then the volume of the prism is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of a Prism = Base Area × Height

Area of Trapezium Base = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Perpendicular distance

Area of Base = 1/2 × (25 + 11) × 16 = 18 × 16 = 288 cm2

Volume = 288 × 10 = 2880 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 2880 cu.cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Parallel sides of the trapezium base (a) = 25 cm and (b) = 11 cm

Distance between parallel sides (hbase) = 16 cm

Height of the prism (H) = 10 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of Right Prism = [1/2 × (a + b) × hbase] × H

Calculations:

⇒ Area of Trapezoidal base = 1/2 × (25 + 11) × 16

⇒ Area of Trapezoidal base = 1/2 × 36 × 16

⇒ Area of Trapezoidal base = 18 × 16 = 288 cm2

⇒ Volume of Prism = Area of base × Height of prism

⇒ Volume = 288 × 10

⇒ Volume = 2880 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 2880 cu.cm.

Additional Information

Surface Area of a Prism

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = Perimeter of base × height. Total Surface Area (TSA) = LSA + 2 × Base Area.

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume of a pyramid with the same base and height as a prism is exactly 1/3 of the volume of the prism (V = 1/3 × Base Area × Height).

Regular Polygon Base

If the base is a regular polygon with side 'a' and 'n' sides, the Area = (n × a2) / [4 × tan(180°/n)].

questions.question: The external and the internal radii of a hollow right circular cylinder of height 15 cm are 6.75 cm and 5.25 cm respectively. If it is melted to form a solid cylinder of height half of the original cylinder, then the radius of the solid cylinder is:
questions.questionHtml: The external and the internal radii of a hollow right circular cylinder of height 15 cm are 6.75 cm and 5.25 cm respectively. If it is melted to form a solid cylinder of height half of the original cylinder, then the radius of the solid cylinder is:

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangular piece of a land area in a ratio 5 : 3. The owner spent Rs. 6000 for surrounding it from all sides at Rs. 7.50 per metre. The difference between its length and breadth is:
questions.questionHtml: The length and breadth of a rectangular piece of a land area in a ratio 5 : 3. The owner spent Rs. 6000 for surrounding it from all sides at Rs. 7.50 per metre. The difference between its length and breadth is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Perimeter = Total Cost ÷ Rate = 6000 ÷ 7.50 = 800 m.

Ratio sum parts for perimeter = 2 × (5 + 3) = 16 units.

16 units = 800 m ⇒ 1 unit = 50 m.

Difference (5 − 3) = 2 units = 2 × 50 = 100 m.

∴ The correct answer is 100 metres.

Alternate Method

Given: Ratio of Length (L) to Breadth (B) = 5 : 3, Cost of fencing = ₹6000, Rate = ₹7.50/m.

Formula Used: Perimeter of rectangle = 2(L + B); Total Cost = Perimeter × Rate.

⇒ Let the Length be 5x and Breadth be 3x.

⇒ Perimeter = Total Cost ÷ Rate per metre

⇒ Perimeter = 6000 ÷ 7.50 = 800 metres.

⇒ According to formula: 2(5x + 3x) = 800

⇒ 2(8x) = 800

⇒ 16x = 800

⇒ x = 800 ÷ 16 = 50.

⇒ Difference between Length and Breadth = 5x − 3x = 2x

⇒ Difference = 2 × 50 = 100 metres.

∴ The correct answer is 100 metres.

Additional Information

Perimeter of Rectangle

The total distance around the rectangle is given by P = 2 × (Length + Breadth).

Area of Rectangle

The surface area enclosed by the rectangle is given by A = Length × Breadth.

Diagonal of Rectangle

The length of the diagonal connecting opposite vertices is d = √(Length2 + Breadth2).

questions.question: The ratio between the area of a square and that of a circle, when the length of a side of the square is equal to that of the diameter of the circle, is: (take π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: The ratio between the area of a square and that of a circle, when the length of a side of the square is equal to that of the diameter of the circle, is: (take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the side of the square be s. Then the diameter of the circle is also s.

Area of Square : Area of Circle = s2 : π × (s/2)2

Ratio = s2 : (π × s2) / 4 = 1 : π/4 = 4 : π

Ratio = 4 : (22/7) = 28 : 22 = 14 : 11.

∴ The correct answer is 14 : 11.

Alternate Method

Given: Side of square (s) = Diameter of circle (d)

Formula: Area of Square = s2 | Area of Circle = πr2 (where r = d/2)

Let the side of the square (s) = 14 units

⇒ Diameter of the circle (d) = 14 units

⇒ Radius of the circle (r) = d ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 units

⇒ Area of the square = s2 = 14 × 14 = 196 sq. units

⇒ Area of the circle = πr2 = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 22 × 7 = 154 sq. units

⇒ Required Ratio = 196 : 154

⇒ Dividing both by 14: 14 : 11

∴ The correct answer is 14 : 11.

Additional Information

Circle Inscribed in a Square

When a circle is inscribed in a square, the diameter of the circle is equal to the side of the square (d = s). The ratio of areas is always 4 : π.

Square Inscribed in a Circle

When a square is inscribed in a circle, the diagonal of the square is equal to the diameter of the circle (s√2 = d). The ratio of area of circle to area of square is π : 2.

Area and Perimeter Formulas

Square Area = s2, Perimeter = 4s. Circle Area = πr2, Circumference = 2πr.

questions.question: A piece of wire 132 cm long is bent successively in the shape of an equilateral triangle, a square and a circle. Then the area will be the largest in the shape of:
questions.questionHtml: A piece of wire 132 cm long is bent successively in the shape of an equilateral triangle, a square and a circle. Then the area will be the largest in the shape of:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a fixed perimeter (constant length of wire), the area of a closed geometric shape increases as the number of sides increases.

Comparing the given shapes: Equilateral Triangle (3 sides) < Square (4 sides) < Circle (limiting case with infinite sides).

Area Hierarchy: Area of Triangle < Area of Square < Area of Circle.

Since the length of the wire is constant at 132 cm, the Circle will always yield the largest area.

∴ The correct answer is Circle.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total length of wire (Perimeter) = 132 cm

Formula Used:

Area of Equilateral Triangle = (√3 / 4) × (side)2

Area of Square = (side)2

Area of Circle = πr2

Calculations:

1. For Equilateral Triangle:

⇒ Side = 132 ÷ 3 = 44 cm

⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × 44 × 44 = 484√3 ≈ 484 × 1.732 ≈ 838.31 cm2

2. For Square:

⇒ Side = 132 ÷ 4 = 33 cm

⇒ Area = 33 × 33 = 1089 cm2

3. For Circle:

⇒ Circumference = 2 × (22 / 7) × r = 132

⇒ r = (132 × 7) / (2 × 22) = 21 cm

⇒ Area = (22 / 7) × 21 × 21 = 22 × 3 × 21 = 1386 cm2

Comparing the areas: 1386 cm2 (Circle) > 1089 cm2 (Square) > 838.31 cm2 (Triangle).

∴ The correct answer is Circle.

Additional Information

Isoperimetric Property

Among all closed curves of a given length, the circle encloses the maximum area. This is a fundamental principle in geometry.

Area of Regular Polygon

For a regular polygon with n sides and perimeter P, Area = P2 / [4 × n × tan(180°/n)]. As n increases, the area increases and approaches πr2.

Square vs Rectangles

For a constant perimeter, a square has a larger area than any other rectangle. Similarly, for a constant area, the square has the smallest perimeter.

questions.question: Two regular polygons are such that the ratio between their number of sides is 1 : 2 and the ratio of measures of their each interior angle is 3 : 4. Then the number of sides of each polygon is:
questions.questionHtml: Two regular polygons are such that the ratio between their number of sides is 1 : 2 and the ratio of measures of their each interior angle is 3 : 4. Then the number of sides of each polygon is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of sides n1 : n2 = 1 : 2 ⇒ Let sides be n and 2n.

Shortcut for ratio of interior angles of n and 2n sides: (n − 2) / (n − 1) = Ratio.

Here, (n − 2) / (n − 1) = 3 / 4.

Solving for n: 4n − 8 = 3n − 3 ⇒ n = 5.

Number of sides = 5 and 2 × 5 = 10.

∴ The correct answer is 5, 10.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of number of sides = 1 : 2

Ratio of interior angles = 3 : 4

Formula Used:

Measure of each interior angle of a regular polygon with n sides = [(n − 2) × 180] ÷ n

Calculations:

⇒ Let the number of sides of the two polygons be n and 2n respectively.

⇒ Ratio of interior angles = [{(n − 2) × 180} ÷ n] ÷ [{(2n − 2) × 180} ÷ 2n] = 3 ÷ 4

⇒ [(n − 2) ÷ n] × [2n ÷ (2n − 2)] = 3 ÷ 4

⇒ [2(n − 2)] ÷ [2(n − 1)] = 3 ÷ 4

⇒ (n − 2) ÷ (n − 1) = 3 ÷ 4

⇒ 4 × (n − 2) = 3 × (n − 1)

⇒ 4n − 8 = 3n − 3

⇒ 4n − 3n = 8 − 3

⇒ n = 5

⇒ Number of sides of first polygon = 5

⇒ Number of sides of second polygon = 2 × 5 = 10

∴ The correct answer is 5, 10.

Additional Information

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of a polygon with n sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Exterior Angle Property

For any regular polygon, each exterior angle = 360° ÷ n. The sum of interior and exterior angle is always 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon, taking one at each vertex, is always 360°.

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle, the length of each equal side is twice the length of the third side. The ratio of areas of the isosceles triangle and an equilateral triangle with the same perimeter is:
questions.questionHtml: In an isosceles triangle, the length of each equal side is twice the length of the third side. The ratio of areas of the isosceles triangle and an equilateral triangle with the same perimeter is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the third side of the isosceles triangle be x. The equal sides are 2x each.

Perimeter (P) = 2x + 2x + x = 5x. Area of Isosceles = (x/4)√(4(2x)2 − x2) = (x2√15)/4.

Equilateral triangle has same perimeter P = 5x, so side s = 5x/3.

Area of Equilateral = (√3/4) × (5x/3)2 = 25√3x2/36.

Ratio = [(x2√15)/4] : [25√3x2/36] = 9√15 : 25√3 = 9√5 : 25 = 36√5 : 100.

∴ The correct answer is 36√5 : 100.

Alternate Method

Given: Equal sides of isosceles triangle = 2 × Base. Perimeter of isosceles triangle = Perimeter of equilateral triangle.

Let the base of the isosceles triangle be b.

⇒ Equal sides (a) = 2b.

⇒ Perimeter of isosceles triangle = a + a + b = 2b + 2b + b = 5b.

Area of Isosceles triangle = (b/4) × √(4a2 − b2)

⇒ Areaiso = (b/4) × √(4(2b)2 − b2) = (b/4) × √(16b2 − b2) = (b/4) × √15b2 = (b2√15)/4.

Side of equilateral triangle (s) = Perimeter/3 = 5b/3.

Area of Equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × s2

⇒ Areaequi = (√3/4) × (5b/3)2 = (√3/4) × (25b2/9) = (25√3b2)/36.

Ratio of areas = [(b2√15)/4] : [(25√3b2)/36]

⇒ Ratio = (√15/4) : (25√3/36)

⇒ Ratio = (9√15) : (25√3)

⇒ Ratio = (9 × √5 × √3) : (25 × √3)

⇒ Ratio = 9√5 : 25

To match the options, multiply both sides by 4:

⇒ Ratio = (9√5 × 4) : (25 × 4) = 36√5 : 100.

∴ The correct answer is 36√5 : 100.

Additional Information

Area of Isosceles Triangle

For an isosceles triangle with equal sides 'a' and base 'b', the altitude h = √(a2 − (b/2)2) and Area = (b/4)√(4a2 − b2).

Area of Equilateral Triangle

For an equilateral triangle with side 's', all sides are equal and all angles are 60°. Area = (√3/4)s2 and height h = (√3/2)s.

Heron's Formula

Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where s = (a + b + c)/2 is the semi-perimeter and a, b, c are the lengths of the sides.

questions.questionHtml: A right circular cylinder is partially filled with water. Two iron spherical balls are completely immersed in the water so that the height of the water in the cylinder rises by 4 cm. If the radius of one ball is half of the other and the diameter of the cylinder is 18 cm, then the radii of the spherical balls are:
questions.solution:
Let the radii of the spherical balls be r cm and r/2 cm.

Radius of the cylinder R = 18/2 = 9 cm.

According to the question

(4/3) π [r3 + (r/2)3] = π R2 h

⇒ (4/3) [r3 + r3/8] = 9 × 9 × 4

⇒ 9r3/8 = 9 × 9 × 3

⇒ r3 = 9 × 3 × 8

⇒ r = ∛[3 × 3 × 3 × 2 × 2 × 2]

⇒ r = 3 × 2

⇒ r = 6 cm

⇒ r/2 = 3 cm

So, radii of the cylinder are 3 cm and 6 cm.

questions.question: The whole surface area of a pyramid whose base is a regular polygon is 340 cm 2 and area of its base is 100 cm 2 . Area of each lateral face is 30 cm 2 . Then the number of lateral faces is:
questions.questionHtml: The whole surface area of a pyramid whose base is a regular polygon is 340 cm<sup>2</sup> and area of its base is 100 cm<sup>2</sup>. Area of each lateral face is 30 cm<sup>2</sup>. Then the number of lateral faces is:
questions.solution:
Total surface area = Lateral surface area + Area of Base

340 = Lateral surface area + 100

Lateral surface area = 340 – 100 = 240 cm2

Area of each lateral face = 30 cm2

Number of lateral faces = 240/30 = 8

questions.question: If P = 99, then the value of P(P 2 + 3P + 3) is:
questions.questionHtml: If P = 99, then the value of P(P<sup>2</sup> + 3P + 3) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The expression P(P2 + 3P + 3) can be written as P3 + 3P2 + 3P.

Using the algebraic identity (a + b)3 = a3 + 3a2b + 3ab2 + b3, we see that:

(P + 1)3 − 1 = P3 + 3P2 + 3P + 1 − 1 = P3 + 3P2 + 3P.

Substitute P = 99: (99 + 1)3 − 1 = 1003 − 1 = 1,000,000 − 1 = 999,999.

∴ The correct answer is 999999.

Alternate Method

Given: P = 99

Formula Used: (a + b)3 = a3 + 3a2b + 3ab2 + b3

Calculations:

Required value = P(P2 + 3P + 3)

⇒ P3 + 3P2 + 3P

⇒ (P3 + 3P2 + 3P + 1) − 1

⇒ (P + 1)3 − 1

⇒ (99 + 1)3 − 1

⇒ (100)3 − 1

⇒ 1000000 − 1

⇒ 999999

∴ The correct answer is 999999.

Additional Information

Cube of a Sum Identity

(a + b)3 = a3 + 3a2b + 3ab2 + b3. In this problem, putting b = 1 gives a3 + 3a2 + 3a + 1.

Cube of a Difference Identity

(a − b)3 = a3 − 3a2b + 3ab2 − b3. For b = 1, it results in a3 − 3a2 + 3a − 1.

Sum and Difference of Cubes

a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) and a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).

questions.question: If x + 1/x = c + 1/c then the value of x is:
questions.questionHtml: If x + 1/x = c + 1/c then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The equation x + 1/x = c + 1/c is symmetric with respect to x and c.

By inspection, if we substitute x = c, both sides become identical (c + 1/c = c + 1/c).

In reciprocal equations of the form f(x) + 1/f(x) = k, if x is a root, then 1/x is also a root.

By substituting x = 1/c, the equation becomes 1/c + c = c + 1/c, which is also true.

Thus, the two values satisfying the equation are c and its reciprocal 1/c.

∴ The correct answer is c, 1/c.

Alternate Method

Given: x + 1/x = c + 1/c

Formula Used: Quadratic rearrangement and factorisation.

⇒ x − c + 1/x − 1/c = 0

⇒ (x − c) + (c − x) / (cx) = 0

⇒ (x − c) − (x − c) / (cx) = 0

⇒ (x − c) [1 − 1/(cx)] = 0

⇒ (x − c) [(cx − 1) / (cx)] = 0

⇒ x − c = 0 or cx − 1 = 0

⇒ x = c or x = 1/c

∴ The correct answer is c, 1/c.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Equations

Equations where the reciprocal of any root is also a root of the equation. These often take the form x + 1/x = k.

Product of Roots in Reciprocal Form

The equation x + 1/x = a can be written as x2 − ax + 1 = 0. According to Vieta's formulas, the product of roots (c/a) is 1/1 = 1.

Nature of Roots

For a quadratic equation ax2 + bx + c = 0, the roots are real and distinct if the discriminant D = b2 − 4ac > 0.

questions.question: If the sum of squares of two real numbers is 41 and their sum is 9. Then the sum of cubes of these two numbers is:
questions.questionHtml: If the sum of squares of two real numbers is 41 and their sum is 9. Then the sum of cubes of these two numbers is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Test integer pairs whose sum is 9: (1,8), (2,7), (3,6), (4,5).

Check squares: 42 + 52 = 16 + 25 = 41. (Condition satisfied)

Sum of cubes: 43 + 53 = 64 + 125 = 189.

∴ The correct answer is 189.

Alternate Method

Given: Sum of numbers (x + y) = 9

Sum of squares (x2 + y2) = 41

Formula used: (x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy

Formula used: x3 + y3 = (x + y)(x2 + y2 − xy)

⇒ (x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy

⇒ 92 = 41 + 2xy

⇒ 81 = 41 + 2xy

⇒ 2xy = 81 − 41 = 40

⇒ xy = 20

⇒ x3 + y3 = (x + y)(x2 + y2 − xy)

⇒ x3 + y3 = 9 × (41 − 20)

⇒ x3 + y3 = 9 × 21 = 189

∴ The correct answer is 189.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity for Cubes

The sum of cubes can also be written as: x3 + y3 = (x + y)3 − 3xy(x + y).

Difference of Cubes

The identity for the difference of two cubes is: x3 − y3 = (x − y)(x2 + xy + y2).

Product of Numbers

Given the sum and sum of squares, the product of two numbers is always xy = [(x + y)2 − (x2 + y2)] ÷ 2.

questions.question: A complete factorisation of x 4 + 64 is:
questions.questionHtml: A complete factorisation of x<sup>4</sup> + 64 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify the expression as the sum of two squares: x4 + 64 = (x2)2 + 82.

Apply the Sophie Germain Identity: a4 + 4b4 = (a2 + 2b2 + 2ab)(a2 + 2b2 − 2ab).

Here, a = x and 4b4 = 64 ⇒ b4 = 16 ⇒ b = 2.

Substituting values: (x2 + 2 × 22 + 2 × x × 2)(x2 + 2 × 22 − 2 × x × 2).

Simplifying the terms: (x2 + 8 + 4x)(x2 + 8 − 4x) → (x2 + 4x + 8)(x2 − 4x + 8).

∴ The correct answer is (x2 + 4x + 8)(x2 − 4x + 8).

Alternate Method

Given: x4 + 64

Formula Used: a2 + b2 = (a + b)2 − 2ab and a2 − b2 = (a + b)(a − b)

⇒ x4 + 64 = (x2)2 + (8)2 ⇒ (x2 + 8)2 − 2 × x2 × 8 ⇒ (x2 + 8)2 − 16x2 ⇒ (x2 + 8)2 − (4x)2 ⇒ Using the difference of squares identity where a = (x2 + 8) and b = 4x ⇒ (x2 + 8 + 4x)(x2 + 8 − 4x) ⇒ (x2 + 4x + 8)(x2 − 4x + 8)

∴ The correct answer is (x2 + 4x + 8)(x2 − 4x + 8).

Additional Information

Sophie Germain Identity

The identity states that a4 + 4b4 = (a2 + 2b2 + 2ab)(a2 + 2b2 − 2ab). This is useful for factorizing sums of even powers.

Difference of Two Squares

For any two terms, a2 − b2 = (a − b)(a + b). It is a fundamental tool in polynomial factorization.

Perfect Square Trinomial

Expanding (a + b)2 gives a2 + 2ab + b2. In this problem, we added and subtracted the middle term 16x2 to create this form.

questions.question: If a + b = 1, then a 4 + b 4 – a 3 – b 3 – 2a 2 b 2 + ab is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If a + b = 1, then a<sup>4</sup> + b<sup>4</sup> – a<sup>3</sup> – b<sup>3</sup> – 2a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>2</sup> + ab is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For algebraic identities given with a condition like a + b = 1, use the value substitution method.

Let a = 1 and b = 0, which satisfies the condition 1 + 0 = 1.

Substitute these values into the expression: 14 + 04 − 13 − 03 − 2(12 × 02) + (1 × 0)

⇒ 1 + 0 − 1 − 0 − 0 + 0 = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method

Given: a + b = 1

Expression: a4 + b4 − a3 − b3 − 2a2b2 + ab

Step 1: Rearrange and group the terms.

⇒ (a4 + b4 − 2a2b2) − (a3 + b3) + ab

Step 2: Apply the identity (x2 − y2)2 = x4 + y4 − 2x2y2 and the sum of cubes identity.

⇒ (a2 − b2)2 − (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) + ab

Step 3: Since a + b = 1, substitute this value into the expression.

⇒ [(a + b)(a − b)]2 − (1)(a2 − ab + b2) + ab

⇒ (1 × (a − b))2 − a2 + ab − b2 + ab

⇒ (a − b)2 − a2 + 2ab − b2

Step 4: Expand (a − b)2.

⇒ (a2 − 2ab + b2) − a2 + 2ab − b2

⇒ 0

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Sum and Difference of Cubes

a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) and a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).

Basic Algebraic Identities

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab and (a − b)2 = a2 + b2 − 2ab.

Value Substitution Method

In competitive exams, if an expression is true for a given condition, substituting simple values (like 0, 1, −1) that satisfy the condition often yields the answer quickly.

questions.question: If x 2 + y 2 + 6x + 5 = 4(x – y) then x – y is:
questions.questionHtml: If x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + 6x + 5 = 4(x – y) then x – y is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify perfect squares by rearranging: x2 + 2x + 1 + y2 + 4y + 4 = 0.

The equation simplifies to: (x + 1)2 + (y + 2)2 = 0.

For the sum of squares of real numbers to be zero, each square must be zero.

∴ x + 1 = 0 → x = −1 and y + 2 = 0 → y = −2.

Then, x − y = −1 − (−2) = −1 + 2 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given: x2 + y2 + 6x + 5 = 4(x − y)

Formula used: (a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2

⇒ x2 + y2 + 6x + 5 = 4x − 4y

⇒ x2 + 6x − 4x + y2 + 4y + 5 = 0

⇒ x2 + 2x + y2 + 4y + 5 = 0

⇒ (x2 + 2x + 1) + (y2 + 4y + 4) = 0

⇒ (x + 1)2 + (y + 2)2 = 0

Since the sum of squares is zero, each base must be zero independently:

⇒ x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = −1

⇒ y + 2 = 0 ⇒ y = −2

⇒ x − y = (−1) − (−2) = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Sum of Squares Property

If a2 + b2 + c2 + ... = 0 for real numbers, then a = b = c = ... = 0.

Perfect Square Identities

(a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2 and (a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2 are fundamental in completing the square.

Quadratic Expressions

To complete the square for x2 + kx, add and subtract (k/2)2.

questions.question: If a = 299, b = 298, c = 297 then the value of 2a 3 + 2b 3 + 2c 3 – 6abc is:
questions.questionHtml: If a = 299, b = 298, c = 297 then the value of 2a<sup>3</sup> + 2b<sup>3</sup> + 2c<sup>3</sup> – 6abc is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If numbers a, b, and c are in Arithmetic Progression (AP) with common difference d, then a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 9 × middle term × d2.

Here a = 299, b = 298, c = 297 are in AP with middle term b = 298 and common difference d = 1.

The given expression is 2 × (a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc).

Value = 2 × (9 × 298 × 12) = 18 × 298 = 5364.

∴ The correct answer is 5364.

Alternate Method

Given: a = 299, b = 298, c = 297

Formula used: a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = ½(a + b + c)[(a − b)2 + (b − c)2 + (c − a)2]

⇒ Required expression = 2a3 + 2b3 + 2c3 − 6abc = 2(a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc)

⇒ Value = 2 × ½ × (a + b + c)[(a − b)2 + (b − c)2 + (c − a)2]

⇒ Value = (a + b + c)[(a − b)2 + (b − c)2 + (c − a)2]

⇒ Sum (a + b + c) = 299 + 298 + 297 = 894

⇒ Differences: (a − b) = 1, (b − c) = 1, (c − a) = −2

⇒ Value = 894 × [12 + 12 + (−2)2]

⇒ Value = 894 × [1 + 1 + 4] = 894 × 6

⇒ Value = 5364

∴ The correct answer is 5364.

Additional Information

Standard Algebraic Identity

The expansion of a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc is (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ca).

Sum of Squares Relation

The term (a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ca) can also be written as ½[(a − b)2 + (b − c)2 + (c − a)2].

Special Conditional Property

If (a + b + c) = 0 or if a = b = c, then the value of a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 0, which implies a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = √3, then the value of x 18 + x 12 + x 6 + 1 is:
questions.questionHtml: If x + 1/x = √3, then the value of x<sup>18</sup> + x<sup>12</sup> + x<sup>6</sup> + 1 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If x + 1/x = √3, then the property x6 = −1 (or x6 + 1 = 0) is always satisfied.

For any two terms xn and xm where the difference between powers |n − m| = 6, their sum is 0.

The given expression is x18 + x12 + x6 + 1.

Grouping the terms: (x18 + x12) + (x6 + 1) = x12(x6 + 1) + (x6 + 1).

Substituting x6 + 1 = 0: (x12 × 0) + 0 = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method

Given: x + 1/x = √3

Formula Used: (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ Cubing both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (x + 1/x)3 = (√3)3

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 + 3 × x × (1/x) × (x + 1/x) = 3√3

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 + 3 × (√3) = 3√3

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 3√3 − 3√3 = 0

⇒ (x6 + 1) / x3 = 0 ⇒ x6 + 1 = 0 ⇒ x6 = −1

⇒ Now, substitute x6 = −1 in the expression x18 + x12 + x6 + 1:

⇒ (x6)3 + (x6)2 + (x6)1 + 1

⇒ (−1)3 + (−1)2 + (−1) + 1

⇒ −1 + 1 − 1 + 1 = 0

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Special Case: x + 1/x = 1

If x + 1/x = 1, then x3 + 1 = 0, which implies x3 = −1.

Special Case: x + 1/x = −1

If x + 1/x = −1, then x3 − 1 = 0, which implies x3 = 1.

Special Case: x + 1/x = √2

If x + 1/x = √2, then x4 + 1 = 0, which implies x4 = −1.

General Result for √3

When x + 1/x = √3, any expression of the form xn + xn-6 + xm + xm-6 + ... will always result in 0.

questions.question: If x = 1 + √2 + √3, then the value of 2x 4 – 8x 3 – 5x 2 + 26x – 28 is:
questions.questionHtml: If x = 1 + √2 + √3, then the value of 2x<sup>4</sup> – 8x<sup>3</sup> – 5x<sup>2</sup> + 26x – 28 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rearrange x = 1 + √2 + √3 to (x − 1)2 = (√2 + √3)2 ⇒ x2 − 2x − 4 = 2√6.

Square again: (x2 − 2x − 4)2 = 24 ⇒ x4 − 4x3 − 4x2 + 16x − 8 = 0.

Multiply by 2: 2x4 − 8x3 − 8x2 + 32x − 16 = 0.

Target expression = (2x4 − 8x3 − 8x2 + 32x − 16) + 3(x2 − 2x − 4).

Substitute values: 0 + 3(2√6) = 6√6.

∴ The correct answer is 6√6.

Alternate Method

Given: x = 1 + √2 + √3

Formula: (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca

⇒ x − 1 = √2 + √3

⇒ (x − 1)2 = (√2 + √3)2

⇒ x2 − 2x + 1 = 2 + 3 + 2√6

⇒ x2 − 2x − 4 = 2√6

⇒ (x2 − 2x − 4)2 = (2√6)2

⇒ x4 + 4x2 + 16 + 2(x2)(−2x) + 2(−2x)(−4) + 2(x2)(−4) = 24

⇒ x4 + 4x2 + 16 − 4x3 + 16x − 8x2 = 24

⇒ x4 − 4x3 − 4x2 + 16x − 8 = 0

Now, rewrite the given expression: 2x4 − 8x3 − 5x2 + 26x − 28

⇒ 2(x4 − 4x3 − 4x2 + 16x − 8) + 8x2 − 32x + 16 − 5x2 + 26x − 28

⇒ 2(0) + 3x2 − 6x − 12

⇒ 3(x2 − 2x − 4)

⇒ 3 × 2√6 = 6√6

∴ The correct answer is 6√6.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identities

Expansion of (a + b + c)2 is a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca. This is vital for solving equations with multiple radicals.

Rationalization and Polynomials

If a variable equals a sum of surds, repeated squaring can transform it into a polynomial with integer coefficients equal to zero.

Remainder Theorem

For any polynomial P(x), if we find a divisor D(x) such that D(x) = 0, then the value of P(x) is simply the remainder R(x) when P(x) is divided by D(x).

questions.question: If \(2r=h+\sqrt{{{r}^{2}}+{{h}^{2}}}\) then the ratio r : h (r ≠ 0) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(2r=h+\sqrt{{{r}^{2}}+{{h}^{2}}}\) then the ratio r : h (r ≠ 0) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Test the ratio options directly in the equation 2r − h = √(r2 + h2).

For Option (3) 4 : 3, let r = 4 and h = 3.

LHS = 2(4) − 3 = 8 − 3 = 5.

RHS = √(42 + 32) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5.

Since LHS = RHS, the ratio r : h = 4 : 3 is the correct solution.

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 3.

Alternate Method

Given: 2r = h + √(r2 + h2)

⇒ 2r − h = √(r2 + h2)

Squaring both sides:

⇒ (2r − h)2 = (√(r2 + h2))2

⇒ 4r2 + h2 − 4rh = r2 + h2

⇒ 4r2 − r2 = 4rh

⇒ 3r2 = 4rh

Dividing both sides by rh (since r ≠ 0 and h ≠ 0):

⇒ 3r/h = 4

⇒ r/h = 4/3

⇒ r : h = 4 : 3

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 3.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity

(a − b)2 = a2 + b2 − 2ab. This is used to expand terms when solving equations involving radicals.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers a, b, and c such that a2 + b2 = c2. Examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Ratio and Proportion

If x/y = a/b, then x : y = a : b. Ratios represent the relative size of two quantities and are independent of actual units.

questions.question: In an equilateral triangle ABC, G is the centroid. Each side of the triangle is 6 cm. The length of AG is:
questions.questionHtml: In an equilateral triangle ABC, G is the centroid. Each side of the triangle is 6 cm. The length of AG is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In an equilateral triangle, the distance from the vertex to the centroid (AG) is equal to the circumradius (R).

Shortcut Formula: AG = side / √3

Given: side = 6 cm

⇒ AG = 6 / √3 = (2 × 3) / √3 = 2√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of equilateral triangle ABC (a) = 6 cm

G = Centroid of the triangle

Formula Used:

Height (h) of equilateral triangle = (√3 / 2) × a

Distance from vertex to centroid (AG) = (2/3) × Height

Calculations:

⇒ Height (AD) = (√3 / 2) × 6

⇒ AD = 3√3 cm

⇒ In an equilateral triangle, the centroid G divides the altitude AD in the ratio 2 : 1.

⇒ AG = (2 / 3) × AD

⇒ AG = (2 / 3) × 3√3

⇒ AG = 2√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.

Additional Information

Height and Area of Equilateral Triangle

The height (h) is given by (√3/2) × a and the area is given by (√3/4) × a2, where 'a' is the side.

Circumradius and Inradius

For an equilateral triangle, the circumradius (R) is a/√3 and the inradius (r) is a/(2√3). Note that R = 2r.

Centroid Property

The centroid G of any triangle divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex to the base.

questions.question: PQ is a tangent to the circle at T. If TR = TS where, R and S are points on the circle and ∠RST = 65°, the ∠PTS = ?
questions.questionHtml: PQ is a tangent to the circle at T. If TR = TS where, R and S are points on the circle and ∠RST = 65°, the ∠PTS = ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In ΔTRS, given TR = TS and ∠RST = 65°, so ∠TRS = ∠RST = 65°.

By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between the tangent QT and chord TS is equal to the angle in the alternate segment, ∠TRS.

⇒ ∠QTS = ∠TRS = 65°.

Since PQ is a straight line tangent at T, ∠PTS = 180° − ∠QTS = 180° − 65° = 115°.

∴ The correct answer is 115°.

Alternate Method

Given: ∠RST = 65°, TR = TS, PQ is a tangent at T.

Formula Used: Alternate Segment Theorem; Angle sum property of triangle; Angles opposite to equal sides in a triangle are equal.

Calculations:

⇒ In ΔTRS, TR = TS (Given)

⇒ ∠TRS = ∠TSR = 65° (Angles opposite to equal sides are equal)

⇒ In ΔTRS, ∠RTS + ∠TRS + ∠TSR = 180° (Angle sum property)

⇒ ∠RTS + 65° + 65° = 180°

⇒ ∠RTS = 180° − 130° = 50°

⇒ According to the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between tangent PT and chord TR is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠PTR = ∠TSR = 65°

⇒ ∠PTS = ∠PTR + ∠RTS

⇒ ∠PTS = 65° + 50° = 115°

∴ The correct answer is 115°.

Additional Information

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a chord and a tangent through one of the end points of the chord is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

Isosceles Triangle Property

In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are always equal in measure.

Tangents to a Circle

A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. From an external point, exactly two tangents can be drawn to a circle, and they are equal in length.

questions.question: In ΔABC, AC = BC and ∠ABC = 50°, the side BC is produced to D so that BC = CD then the value of ∠BAD is:
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, AC = BC and ∠ABC = 50°, the side BC is produced to D so that BC = CD then the value of ∠BAD is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given $AC = BC$ and $BC = CD$, we have $AC = BC = CD$.

This implies point $C$ is equidistant from points $A, B,$ and $D$.

Thus, $C$ is the circumcenter of $\triangle ABD$, making $BD$ the diameter of its circumcircle.

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always $90°$.

∴ The correct answer is 90°.

Alternate Method

Given: $AC = BC$, $\angle ABC = 50°$, and $BC = CD$.

Formula Used: Angle sum property of a triangle and Isosceles triangle property (angles opposite to equal sides are equal).

⇒ In $\triangle ABC$, $AC = BC$ ⇒ $\angle BAC = \angle ABC = 50°$.

⇒ In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 180° − (\angle BAC + \angle ABC) = 180° − (50° + 50°) = 80°$.

⇒ Since $BCD$ is a straight line, $\angle ACD = 180° − \angle ACB = 180° − 80° = 100°$.

⇒ Given $BC = CD$ and $AC = BC$ ⇒ $AC = CD$.

⇒ In $\triangle ACD$, $AC = CD$ ⇒ $\angle CAD = \angle CDA = (180° − 100°) \div 2 = 40°$.

⇒ $\angle BAD = \angle BAC + \angle CAD = 50° + 40° = 90°$.

∴ The correct answer is 90°.

Additional Information

Isosceles Triangle Theorem

If two sides of a triangle are equal, then the angles opposite to those sides are also equal.

Angle in a Semicircle

According to Thales's Theorem, the angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of a circle is always $90°$.

Exterior Angle Property

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two interior opposite angles.

questions.question: In a circle, a diameter AB and a chord PQ (which is not a diameter) intersect each other at X perpendicularly. If AX : BX = 3 : 2 and the radius of the circle is 5 cm, then the length of chord PQ is
questions.questionHtml: In a circle, a diameter AB and a chord PQ (which is not a diameter) intersect each other at X perpendicularly. If AX : BX = 3 : 2 and the radius of the circle is 5 cm, then the length of chord PQ is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius = 5 cm → Diameter AB = 10 cm.

Divide AB in ratio 3 : 2 ⇒ AX = 6 cm and BX = 4 cm.

Since diameter AB is perpendicular to chord PQ, X is the midpoint of PQ.

By Intersecting Chords Theorem: (PQ/2)2 = AX × BX.

(PQ/2)2 = 6 × 4 = 24 ⇒ PQ/2 = √24 = 2√6.

PQ = 2 × 2√6 = 4√6 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 4√6 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius (r) = 5 cm ⇒ Diameter (AB) = 10 cm.

Ratio AX : BX = 3 : 2.

Formula used:

1. Intersecting Chords Theorem: AX × BX = PX × XQ.

2. A radius perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord: PX = XQ.

Calculations:

⇒ Total length of diameter AB = 10 cm.

⇒ AX = (3 / (3 + 2)) × 10 = (3/5) × 10 = 6 cm.

⇒ BX = (2 / (3 + 2)) × 10 = (2/5) × 10 = 4 cm.

⇒ Since AB ⊥ PQ, X is the midpoint of PQ ⇒ PX = XQ.

⇒ PX × XQ = AX × BX

⇒ PX2 = 6 × 4 = 24

⇒ PX = √24 = 2√6 cm.

⇒ Length of chord PQ = PX + XQ = 2 × PX = 2 × 2√6 = 4√6 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 4√6 cm.

Additional Information

Intersecting Chords Theorem

When two chords AB and PQ intersect at point X inside a circle, then AX × BX = PX × XQ.

Perpendicular Bisector Property

A line drawn from the center of a circle perpendicular to a chord always bisects that chord into two equal segments.

Pythagoras in Circles

For a chord of length L at distance d from the center of a circle with radius r, the relation is r2 = d2 + (L/2)2.

questions.question: ABC is a triangle, PQ is line segment intersecting AB in P and AC in Q and PQ II BC. The ratio of AP : BP = 3 : 5 and length of PQ is 18 cm. The length of BC is:
questions.questionHtml: ABC is a triangle, PQ is line segment intersecting AB in P and AC in Q and PQ II BC. The ratio of AP : BP = 3 : 5 and length of PQ is 18 cm. The length of BC is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In ▵ABC, since PQ || BC, ▵APQ ∼ ▵ABC.

The ratio of sides is AP : AB = AP : (AP + BP) = 3 : (3 + 5) = 3 : 8.

By similarity, PQ ÷ BC = AP ÷ AB.

18 ÷ BC = 3 ÷ 8.

BC = (18 × 8) ÷ 3 = 6 × 8 = 48 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: In ▵ABC, PQ || BC. AP : BP = 3 : 5 and PQ = 18 cm.

Formula: If PQ || BC, then ▵APQ ∼ ▵ABC (AA similarity).

⇒ AP ÷ AB = PQ ÷ BC

⇒ AB = AP + BP

⇒ AB = 3 + 5 = 8 units (Letting AP = 3 units and BP = 5 units)

⇒ 3 ÷ 8 = 18 ÷ BC

⇒ 3 × BC = 18 × 8

⇒ BC = 144 ÷ 3

⇒ BC = 48 cm

∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.

Additional Information

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio: AP ÷ PB = AQ ÷ QC.

Ratio of Areas of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(▵APQ) ÷ Area(▵ABC) = (AP ÷ AB)2.

Midpoint Theorem

If P and Q are the midpoints of AB and AC respectively, then PQ is parallel to BC and PQ = 1 ÷ 2 × BC.

questions.question: If the parallel sides of a trapezium are 8 cm and 4 cm, M and N are the midpoints of the diagonals of the trapezium, then the length of MN is:
questions.questionHtml: If the parallel sides of a trapezium are 8 cm and 4 cm, M and N are the midpoints of the diagonals of the trapezium, then the length of MN is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The length of the line segment joining the midpoints of the diagonals of a trapezium is half the difference of its parallel sides.

Length MN = (Longer parallel side − Shorter parallel side) ÷ 2

MN = (8 cm − 4 cm) ÷ 2

MN = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: Parallel sides AB = 8 cm and CD = 4 cm. M and N are midpoints of diagonals AC and BD.

Formula: Length of the line joining midpoints of diagonals = (Difference of parallel sides) ÷ 2

⇒ Parallel side 1 (a) = 8 cm

⇒ Parallel side 2 (b) = 4 cm

⇒ Length MN = (a − b) ÷ 2

⇒ MN = (8 − 4) ÷ 2

⇒ MN = 4 ÷ 2

⇒ MN = 2 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.

Additional Information

Median of a Trapezium

The line segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides is called the median and its length is equal to (a + b) ÷ 2.

Area of a Trapezium

The area is calculated as Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height.

Property of Diagonals

In a trapezium, the diagonals divide each other in the same ratio as the ratio of the parallel sides.

questions.question: ΔABC is isosceles having AB = AC and ∠A = 40°. Bisectors PO and OQ of the exterior angles ∠ABD and ∠ACE formed by producing BC on both sides, meet at O. The value of ∠BOC is:
questions.questionHtml: ΔABC is isosceles having AB = AC and ∠A = 40°. Bisectors PO and OQ of the exterior angles ∠ABD and ∠ACE formed by producing BC on both sides, meet at O. The value of ∠BOC is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The point O is the ex-center of ΔABC opposite to vertex A.

The angle formed by the exterior angle bisectors is given by the formula: ∠BOC = 90° − (∠A ÷ 2)

Given ∠A = 40°

∠BOC = 90° − (40° ÷ 2) = 90° − 20° = 70°.

∴ The correct answer is 70°.

Alternate Method

Given: AB = AC, ∠A = 40°, BO and CO are exterior angle bisectors.

In ΔABC, sum of angles = 180°

⇒ ∠A + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°

Since AB = AC, ∠ABC = ∠ACB

⇒ 40° + 2 × ∠ABC = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠ABC = 140° ⇒ ∠ABC = 70° and ∠ACB = 70°

Exterior ∠ABD = 180° − ∠ABC = 180° − 70° = 110°

Exterior ∠ACE = 180° − ∠ACB = 180° − 70° = 110°

Since BO and CO are bisectors:

⇒ ∠OBC = ∠ABD ÷ 2 = 110° ÷ 2 = 55°

⇒ ∠OCB = ∠ACE ÷ 2 = 110° ÷ 2 = 55°

In ΔBOC:

⇒ ∠BOC + ∠OBC + ∠OCB = 180°

⇒ ∠BOC + 55° + 55° = 180°

⇒ ∠BOC + 110° = 180°

⇒ ∠BOC = 180° − 110° = 70°

∴ The correct answer is 70°.

Additional Information

Interior Angle Bisector

The angle formed by the intersection of internal bisectors of ∠B and ∠C is 90° + ∠A/2.

Ex-center Property

The intersection of two exterior angle bisectors and one interior angle bisector (from the third vertex) is called the ex-center.

Sum of External Bisectors

The angle between internal bisector and external bisector of the same vertex is always 90°.

questions.question: An equilateral triangle of side 6 cm is inscribed in a circle,then the radius of the circle is:
questions.questionHtml: An equilateral triangle of side 6 cm is inscribed in a circle,then the radius of the circle is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For an equilateral triangle of side 'a', the circumradius (R) is calculated as R = a ÷ √3.

Given side a = 6 cm.

R = 6 ÷ √3 = (2 × 3) ÷ √3 = 2√3 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: Side of equilateral triangle (a) = 6 cm.

Formula Used: Radius of the circumcircle (R) = Side / √3

⇒ Circumradius (R) = 6 / √3

⇒ Rationalizing the denominator: R = (6 × √3) / (√3 × √3)

⇒ R = 6√3 / 3

⇒ R = 2√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.

Additional Information

Inradius of Equilateral Triangle

The radius of the inscribed circle (inradius) is r = a / (2√3). The circumradius R is always twice the inradius (R = 2r).

Height of Equilateral Triangle

The height (h) is given by h = (√3/2) × a. The circumradius (R) is also equal to 2/3 of the height (R = 2/3 × h).

Area of Equilateral Triangle

The area is calculated as A = (√3/4) × a2, where 'a' is the length of the side.

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, AB is diameter and CD is a chord which is equal to the radius OC. AC and BD are extended in such a way that they intersect each other at a point P, exterior to the circle. The measure of ∠APB is:
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, AB is diameter and CD is a chord which is equal to the radius OC. AC and BD are extended in such a way that they intersect each other at a point P, exterior to the circle. The measure of ∠APB is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Measure of Arc AB = 180° (since AB is the diameter).

Chord CD = Radius ⇒ ∠COD = 60° ⇒ Measure of Arc CD = 60°.

Angle formed by two secants intersecting outside = (Major Arc − Minor Arc) ÷ 2.

∠APB = (Arc AB − Arc CD) ÷ 2 = (180° − 60°) ÷ 2 = 60°.

∴ The correct answer is 60°.

Alternate Method

Given: O is the centre, AB is the diameter, and chord CD = radius OC = OD.

Formula: Angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended at the circumference.

⇒ In ▵COD, OC = OD = CD (all are equal to radius).

⇒ ∴ ▵COD is an equilateral triangle ⇒ ∠COD = 60°.

⇒ Angle at circumference ∠CAD = ∠COD ÷ 2 = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°.

⇒ ∠ADB = 90° (Angle subtended by diameter AB in a semi-circle).

⇒ In ▵PAD, ∠ADB is an exterior angle to the triangle.

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠PAD + ∠APD

⇒ 90° = 30° + ∠APB

⇒ ∠APB = 90° − 30° = 60°.

∴ The correct answer is 60°.

Additional Information

Angle in a Semi-circle

An angle subtended by the diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).

Central Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is twice the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Intersecting Secants Theorem

The angle formed by two secants intersecting outside a circle is half the positive difference of the measures of the intercepted arcs: ∠P = (Arc1 − Arc2) ÷ 2.

questions.question: Two chords AB and CD of a circle with centre O intersect at P. If ∠APC = 40°,then the value of ∠AOC + ∠BOD is:
questions.questionHtml: Two chords AB and CD of a circle with centre O intersect at P. If ∠APC = 40°,then the value of ∠AOC + ∠BOD is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The angle between two intersecting chords inside a circle is half the sum of the angles subtended by the intercepted arcs at the center.

Angle between chords (∠APC) = (∠AOC + ∠BOD) ÷ 2

Given ∠APC = 40°

⇒ 40° = (∠AOC + ∠BOD) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠AOC + ∠BOD = 40° × 2 = 80°

∴ The correct answer is 80°.

Alternate Method

Given: Chords AB and CD intersect at P. O is the center. ∠APC = 40°.

Join AD. In ▵APD:

⇒ ∠APC is the exterior angle to ▵APD.

⇒ ∠APC = ∠PAD + ∠PDA

⇒ ∠PAD is the angle subtended by arc BD at the circumference, so ∠PAD = ∠BOD ÷ 2

⇒ ∠PDA is the angle subtended by arc AC at the circumference, so ∠PDA = ∠AOC ÷ 2

Substituting these in the exterior angle equation:

⇒ ∠APC = (∠BOD ÷ 2) + (∠AOC ÷ 2)

⇒ 40° = (∠BOD + ∠AOC) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠AOC + ∠BOD = 40° × 2

⇒ ∠AOC + ∠BOD = 80°

∴ The correct answer is 80°.

Additional Information

Central Angle Property

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is twice the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the circumference.

Interior Intersecting Chords

When two chords intersect inside a circle, the measure of the angle formed is half the sum of the measures of the intercepted arcs.

Exterior Intersecting Chords

If two chords intersect outside the circle, the angle formed is half the difference of the intercepted arcs.

Power of a Point

For chords AB and CD intersecting at P, the product of segments of the chords is equal: AP × PB = CP × PD.

questions.question: If x tan 60° + cos 45° = sec 45° then the value of x 2 + 1 is:
questions.questionHtml: If x tan 60° + cos 45° = sec 45° then the value of x<sup>2</sup> + 1 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Substitute tan 60° = √3, cos 45° = 1/√2 and sec 45° = √2.

x × √3 + 1/√2 = √2

x√3 = √2 − 1/√2 = 1/√2

x = 1/√6 ⇒ x2 = 1/6

x2 + 1 = 1/6 + 1 = 7/6

∴ The correct answer is 7/6.

Alternate Method

Given: x tan 60° + cos 45° = sec 45°

Formula Used: Standard trigonometric values: tan 60° = √3, cos 45° = 1/√2, sec 45° = √2

Calculations:

⇒ x(√3) + 1/√2 = √2

⇒ x√3 = √2 − 1/√2

⇒ x√3 = (2 − 1) / √2

⇒ x√3 = 1/√2

⇒ x = 1 / (√3 × √2)

⇒ x = 1 / √6

⇒ x2 = (1/√6)2 = 1/6

⇒ x2 + 1 = 1/6 + 1

⇒ x2 + 1 = 7/6

∴ The correct answer is 7/6.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Table Values

Values for 45°: sin 45° = 1/√2, cos 45° = 1/√2, tan 45° = 1. Values for 60°: sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3.

Reciprocal Identities

Secant is the reciprocal of cosine: sec θ = 1/cos θ. Similarly, cosec θ = 1/sin θ and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental relations: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1; 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ; 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

questions.question: x, y be two acute angles, x + y < 90° and sin(2x - 20°) = cos(2y + 20°), the value of tan(x + y) is:
questions.questionHtml: x, y be two acute angles, x + y < 90° and sin(2x - 20°) = cos(2y + 20°), the value of tan(x + y) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For acute angles, if sin A = cos B, then A + B = 90°.

Here, (2x − 20°) + (2y + 20°) = 90°.

2x + 2y = 90° ⇒ x + y = 45°.

Value required: tan(x + y) = tan 45° = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given:

sin(2x − 20°) = cos(2y + 20°)

x, y are acute angles and x + y < 90°.

Formula Used:

sin θ = cos(90° − θ)

Calculations:

⇒ sin(2x − 20°) = cos(2y + 20°)

⇒ sin(2x − 20°) = sin(90° − (2y + 20°))

⇒ 2x − 20° = 90° − 2y − 20°

⇒ 2x + 2y = 90°

⇒ 2(x + y) = 90°

⇒ x + y = 45°

⇒ tan(x + y) = tan 45°

⇒ tan(x + y) = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Complementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin θ = cos(90° − θ), tan θ = cot(90° − θ), and sec θ = csc(90° − θ). These are used when the sum of angles is 90°.

Standard Trigonometric Values of Tangent

Important values: tan 0° = 0, tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3, and tan 90° is undefined.

Condition for acute angles

An angle θ is said to be acute if 0° < θ < 90°. The sum of two acute angles can be less than, equal to, or greater than 90°.

questions.question: If a 2 sec 2 x - b 2 tan 2 x = c 2 then the value of sec 2 x + tan 2 x is equal to (assume b 2 ≠ a 2 )
questions.questionHtml: If a<sup>2</sup>sec<sup>2</sup>x - b<sup>2</sup>tan<sup>2</sup>x = c<sup>2</sup> then the value of sec<sup>2</sup>x + tan<sup>2</sup>x is equal to (assume b<sup>2</sup> ≠ a<sup>2</sup>)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume a simple value for x, let x = 0°.

Then sec20 = 1 and tan20 = 0.

Substitute in the equation: a2(1) − b2(0) = c2 ⇒ a2 = c2.

The target value to find is: sec20 + tan20 = 1 + 0 = 1.

Check Option 2 with a2 = c2: (b2 + a2 − 2a2) / (b2 − a2) = (b2 − a2) / (b2 − a2) = 1.

∴ The correct answer is (b2 + a2 − 2c2) / (b2 − a2).

Alternate Method

Given: a2sec2x − b2tan2x = c2

Formula used: sec2x = 1 + tan2x

⇒ a2(1 + tan2x) − b2tan2x = c2

⇒ a2 + a2 tan2x − b2 tan2x = c2

⇒ tan2x(a2 − b2) = c2 − a2

⇒ tan2x = (c2 − a2) / (a2 − b2)

⇒ sec2x = 1 + tan2x = 1 + (c2 − a2) / (a2 − b2)

⇒ sec2x = (a2 − b2 + c2 − a2) / (a2 − b2) = (c2 − b2) / (a2 − b2)

⇒ sec2x + tan2x = [ (c2 − b2) + (c2 − a2) ] / (a2 − b2)

⇒ sec2x + tan2x = (2c2 − a2 − b2) / (a2 − b2)

⇒ Multiplying numerator and denominator by −1: (a2 + b2 − 2c2) / (b2 − a2)

∴ The correct answer is (b2 + a2 − 2c2) / (b2 − a2).

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin2x + cos2x = 1, sec2x − tan2x = 1, and csc2x − cot2x = 1.

Substitution Method

For trigonometric expressions, substituting standard angles like 0°, 30°, or 45° can often simplify complex algebraic relations and verify options quickly.

Double Angle Formulas

cos 2x = cos2x − sin2x = 1 − 2sin2x = 2cos2x − 1 = (1 − tan2x) / (1 + tan2x).

questions.question: (1 + sec 20° + cot 70°)(1 - cosec 20° + tan70°) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: (1 + sec 20° + cot 70°)(1 - cosec 20° + tan70°) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Convert angles to 20° using complementary rules: cot 70° = tan 20° and tan 70° = cot 20°.

The expression simplifies to: (1 + tan 20° + sec 20°)(1 + cot 20° − cosec 20°).

Recognize the standard trigonometric identity: (1 + tan θ + sec θ)(1 + cot θ − cosec θ) = 2.

This result is independent of the value of θ.

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Alternate Method

Given: (1 + sec 20° + cot 70°)(1 − cosec 20° + tan 70°)

Formula Used: tan(90° − θ) = cot θ; cot(90° − θ) = tan θ; sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

⇒ Convert 70° to 20°: cot 70° = tan 20° and tan 70° = cot 20°

⇒ Expression = (1 + sec 20° + tan 20°)(1 − cosec 20° + cot 20°)

⇒ = (1 + 1/cos 20° + sin 20°/cos 20°)(1 − 1/sin 20° + cos 20°/sin 20°)

⇒ = [(cos 20° + 1 + sin 20°)/cos 20°] × [(sin 20° − 1 + cos 20°)/sin 20°]

⇒ = [(sin 20° + cos 20° + 1)(sin 20° + cos 20° − 1)] / (sin 20° × cos 20°)

⇒ Using (a+b)(a−b) = a2 − b2: [(sin 20° + cos 20°)2 − 12] / (sin 20° × cos 20°)

⇒ = [sin2 20° + cos2 20° + 2 sin 20° cos 20° − 1] / (sin 20° × cos 20°)

⇒ = [1 + 2 sin 20° cos 20° − 1] / (sin 20° × cos 20°)

⇒ = 2 sin 20° cos 20° / sin 20° cos 20° = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information

Complementary Angle Identities

Trigonometric ratios of complementary angles: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental identities include sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Standard Result

The expression (1 + tan θ + sec θ)(1 + cot θ − cosec θ) always evaluates to 2 for all values of θ where the functions are defined.

questions.question: If tan 4 θ + tan 2 θ = 1 then the value of cos 4 θ + cos 2 θ is:
questions.questionHtml: If tan<sup>4</sup>θ + tan<sup>2</sup>θ = 1 then the value of cos<sup>4</sup>θ + cos<sup>2</sup>θ is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given: tan4θ + tan2θ = 1

Factorize: tan2θ(tan2θ + 1) = 1

Using identity 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ: tan2θ × sec2θ = 1

tan2θ = 1 / sec2θ ⇒ tan2θ = cos2θ

Required value: cos4θ + cos2θ = (tan2θ)2 + tan2θ = tan4θ + tan2θ = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given: tan4θ + tan2θ = 1

Formula Used: sec2θ − tan2θ = 1 and sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

⇒ tan4θ + tan2θ = 1

⇒ tan2θ(tan2θ + 1) = 1

⇒ tan2θ × sec2θ = 1

⇒ (sin2θ / cos2θ) × (1 / cos2θ) = 1

⇒ sin2θ / cos4θ = 1

⇒ sin2θ = cos4θ

⇒ Now, we need to find cos4θ + cos2θ

⇒ Substitute cos4θ = sin2θ in the expression:

⇒ sin2θ + cos2θ

⇒ Since sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

1. sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 | 2. 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ | 3. 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Reciprocal Identities

sec θ = 1 / cos θ and cosec θ = 1 / sin θ. Also, tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and cot θ = cos θ / sin θ.

Complementary Angle Properties

sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, cos(90° − θ) = sin θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

questions.question: The value of 8(sin 6 θ + cos 6 θ) - 12(sin 4 θ + cos 4 θ) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The value of 8(sin<sup>6</sup>θ + cos<sup>6</sup>θ) - 12(sin<sup>4</sup>θ + cos<sup>4</sup>θ) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Value Substitution Method: Since the expression is independent of θ, substitute a convenient value for θ.

Let θ = 0°

sin 0° = 0 and cos 0° = 1

Expression = 8(06 + 16) − 12(04 + 14)

Expression = 8(1) − 12(1) = 8 − 12 = −4

∴ The correct answer is −4.

Alternate Method

Given: 8(sin6θ + cos6θ) − 12(sin4θ + cos4θ)

Formula Used:

1. sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

2. a3 + b3 = (a + b)3 − 3ab(a + b)

3. a2 + b2 = (a + b)2 − 2ab

Applying the identities to the powers of sinθ and cosθ:

⇒ sin4θ + cos4θ = (sin2θ + cos2θ)2 − 2 sin2θ cos2θ

⇒ sin4θ + cos4θ = 1 − 2 sin2θ cos2θ

⇒ sin6θ + cos6θ = (sin2θ + cos2θ)3 − 3 sin2θ cos2θ (sin2θ + cos2θ)

⇒ sin6θ + cos6θ = 1 − 3 sin2θ cos2θ

Substitute these into the main expression:

⇒ 8(1 − 3 sin2θ cos2θ) − 12(1 − 2 sin2θ cos2θ)

⇒ 8 − 24 sin2θ cos2θ − 12 + 24 sin2θ cos2θ

⇒ 8 − 12 = −4

∴ The correct answer is −4.

Additional Information

Fundamental Trigonometric Identity

The most basic identity is sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, which relates the sine and cosine of any angle.

Power Expansion Rules

Higher even powers of sine and cosine can always be expressed in terms of (sin2θ + cos2θ) and the product (sinθcosθ).

Independence of Variable

When a trigonometric expression results in a constant numerical value across all options, it implies the expression is independent of the angle θ.

questions.question: An aeroplane flying horizontally at a height of 3 km. above the ground is observed at a certain point on earth to subtend an angle of 60°. After 15 sec flight, its angle of elevation is changed to 30°. The speed of the aeroplane (taking √3 = 1.732) is:

In ΔABD

⇒ 1 = AB/BD

⇒ BD = AB

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower, vertically erected in the middle of a paddy field, from two points on a horizontal line through the foot of the tower and opposite side of the tower are given to be α and β (α > β). The height of the tower is h unit. A possible distance (in the same unit) between the points is:
questions.questionHtml: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower, vertically erected in the middle of a paddy field, from two points on a horizontal line through the foot of the tower and opposite side of the tower are given to be α and β (α > β). The height of the tower is h unit. A possible distance (in the same unit) between the points is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a tower of height h, if points are on opposite sides with angles α and β:

Distance from foot to first point (d1) = h × cot α

Distance from foot to second point (d2) = h × cot β

Total distance between points = d1 + d2 = h(cot α + cot β)

∴ The correct answer is h(cot α + cot β) unit.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height of the tower = h unit

Angle of elevation from first point (A) = α

Angle of elevation from second point (B) = β

In right-angled triangle formed with point A and tower foot F:

⇒ tan α = height / AF = h / AF

⇒ AF = h / tan α = h cot α

In right-angled triangle formed with point B and tower foot F:

⇒ tan β = height / FB = h / FB

⇒ FB = h / tan β = h cot β

Since points A and B are on opposite sides of the tower:

⇒ Distance AB = AF + FB

⇒ Distance AB = h cot α + h cot β

⇒ Distance AB = h(cot α + cot β)

∴ The correct answer is h(cot α + cot β) unit.

Additional Information

Opposite Side vs Same Side Distance

When points are on the opposite side, distance is h(cot α + cot β). If points are on the same side, distance is h|cot α − cot β|.

Trigonometric Ratios in Heights and Distances

The ratio tan θ = Perpendicular/Base is most commonly used. Note that cot θ = 1/tan θ is equivalent to Base/Perpendicular.

Angle of Elevation and α > β

As the point moves closer to the foot of the tower, the angle of elevation increases. Since α > β, point A is closer to the tower than point B.
